newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-NATAL BLOCKS SMALL MOVE TO CAPE PROVINCE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NATAL BLOCKS SMALL MOVE TO CAPE PROVINCE.

text.p: The Natal Rugby Union (NRU) on Wednesday blocked the attempt by Springbok wing James Small to switch allegiance to Western Province.
NRU chief executive officer Brian van Zyl said the union expected Small to honour his contractual obligations for 1997.
"James has made it quite clear he wants to settle in Cape Town but contractual obligations are contractual obligations," van Zyl told Reuters.

"We met with James on Monday prior to a practice and we informed him that, as far as the NRU was concerned, we would expect him to fulfil his ... obligations ... and that he would be playing for Natal."
Van Zyl admitted that forcing Small, who was born in Cape Town, to stay with Natal could lead to a morale problem in the Natal team.

"That might be the case and I think time will determine how that affects the team -- if it does affect the team. Obviously James's approach to us came as somewhat of a surprise and, as we indicated to James, we were left with no alternative but to make this decision because we don't have a ready replacement for him."
Van Zyl said the NRU received no formal approach from Western Province about a James Small transfer.
"James, I'm sure, is not too happy about the situation but time will tell," he said.

If the transfer had gone ahead, Small would have become the second player in South African rugby history to move following the payment of a transfer fee. Springbok flanker Andre Venter was the first when Transvaal paid Free State 250,000 rand ($54,500) for him earlier this year.
